ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier), Articles L561-1 through L561-32, as amended by Order No. 2020-115 and aligned with EU Directive (EU) 2018/843; UBO register obligations under Article L561-2-2 and implementing Decree No. 2016-1630 of 30 November 2016; registration and transparency rules under Commercial Code (Code de commerce) Articles L232-21-1 et seq.; supervision by ACPR and financial intelligence unit Tracfin.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national identity card of each individual shareholder and manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or competent public officer in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address issued within the last 90 days (utility bill or bank statement) for each shareholder and manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing utility company or licensed bank

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Criminal record certificate or certificate of good conduct for the proposed manager (gérant)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent criminal records authority in the country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and certificate of good standing if a legal entity is a shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registration authority in the jurisdiction of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified French translation (traduction assermentée) of all apostilled documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Court-certified translator registered with a French Cour d'appel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization not required; translation certificate attached

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, and managers against the OFAC SDN list, EU Consolidated Sanctions List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, Tracfin national terrorist financing list, and French PEP database. Enhanced due diligence is required for PEPs from high-risk jurisdictions and for politically exposed family members or close associates. Any suspicious activity must be reported to Tracfin under Article L561-15 of the French Monetary and Financial Code.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) with name availability verified through Infogreffe (infogreffe.fr) and the INPI trademark database (base-marques.inpi.fr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A French SARL may adopt a name in any language provided that it is expressed in Latin characters; names in non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into the French commercial register. The name must be distinguishable from existing RCS entries and protected trademarks, must not mislead as to the nature of the business, and must comply with French public order. The legal form 'société à responsabilité limitée' or the abbreviation 'SARL' must appear in all formal documents.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is rejected by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce on grounds of confusion, public order, or lack of distinctiveness, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal with the same Greffe within 15 days of notification, invoking Articles L123-27 and R123-90 of the French Commercial Code. The appeal must set out the distinguishing elements and evidence of non-confusion. The supervising judge (juge commis à la surveillance du registre) shall decide within one month. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may either submit a new name or file an annulment action before the competent Tribunal Judiciaire within two months. A 30-day name reservation may be renewed once at the sole discretion of the Greffe upon written request and applicable fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for an e-commerce SARL. The registered office may be domiciliated through a prefecture-approved commercial domiciliation agency (domiciliataire agréé) under Articles L123-11-2 and R123-166 of the French Commercial Code. The domiciliataire must maintain a physical office in France, accept and forward correspondence, and provide a genuine business address. A mere mail-forwarding point without a supervised French office is not compliant for tax registration or for Stripe/PayPal merchant account underwriting requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate risk of approximately 10% during the first three years for a digital-only pet supplies retailer. Unannounced on-site inspections are more likely if VAT turnover exceeds EUR 1 million, if the domiciliation agency attracts adverse audit attention, or if discrepancies are identified between the declared registered office and observable online business operations. Routine pre-incorporation inspections are typically administrative rather than physical.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark per document page plus statutory apostille fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Included in the greffe registration tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a Paris or major commercial court jurisdiction address

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Code de commerce (French Commercial Code), Articles L. 223-1 et seq. for Société à Responsabilité Limitée
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte de constitution de la société
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital of 1 EUR; no escrow account required
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The undersigned shareholders of the proposed Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL) hereby adopt the following resolutions unanimously: 1. The initial share capital of the Company is subscribed in full by the shareholders in the proportions set forth in the articles of association. 2. The registered office of the Company is adopted at the address specified in the articles of association, located in France. 3. The following officers are appointed: [Name] as Gérant (Manager) with full powers of management and representation, [Name] as Deputy Gérant, and [Name] as Commissaire aux Comptes. The purpose of the Company is the electronic retailing of pet supplies and pet care devices. This resolution is adopted in accordance with the proposed articles and shall be recorded in the minutes of the first meeting of the board. The Company is incorporated upon filing with the registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Notarize Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet-Entreprises.fr or direct submission to Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare notarized draft articles of association including company name, purpose, capital, managers' powers and representation. Submit original signed by all shareholders together with identification documents and payment receipt via the official online portal or in person at the registry office.
required_dossiers: Shareholders identification documents and proof of address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Provide additional documents or request hearing within 15-day statutory period

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: N/A - No industrial licensing required for electronic retail activities
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: N/A - No physical premises or manufacturing operations

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), business tax portal: impots.gouv.fr; VAT and corporate tax files administered by the local Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) within the SIRENE/RNE public registry (sirene.fr); company incorporation, SIREN/SIRET issuance and all statutory formalities operate through the Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises, managed by INPI at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; customs and EORI functions are handled by the Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI) via the DELTA-X export platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 — Formation: file the SARL incorporation dossier through the Guichet unique (INPI); upon validation, INSEE issues the 9-digit SIREN and a 14-digit SIRET establishment code automatically through the Registre National des Entreprises (RNE). Step 2 — Registration: the DGFiP allocates the tax status and activates the business VAT file; the company obtains the numéro de TVA intracommunautaire (format FR + 2-digit control key + 9-digit SIREN) for intra-EU B2B invoicing, export declarations, and VAT refund claims. There is no statutory registration threshold for an established French SARL: registration is mandatory from the first taxable transaction. A de minimis domestic-only trader may alternatively benefit from the franchise en base de TVA (turnover exemption) below EUR 85,000 for goods (Art. 293 B CGI), although an e-commerce pet-supplies SARL will normally waive it. Step 3 — Customs identity: apply to the DGDDI for the EORI number (format FR + SIREN) required to lodge export declarations. Step 4 — Portal activation: create the professional account on impots.gouv.fr (espace professionnel) to file VAT returns (CA3/CA12 via EFI), corporate income tax forms (2065/2072), and refund claims.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (SARL exercising the option for Impôt sur les Sociétés (IS) or SARL with at least one corporate shareholder, which is subject to IS by law; applies the territorial scope of France including permanent-establishment nexus under Art. 209 CGI; no Tax_Exempt_Zone relief applies to this metropolitan retail scope — overseas-department zone regimes such as La Réunion (8.5% VAT) are N/A for a standard metropolitan SARL).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: French law does not apply a US-style check-the-box regime; the available characterization elections are: (i) irrevocable option for corporate income tax (IS) by a SARL whose members are exclusively natural persons (Art. 3-bis CGI, first sentence), converting the default income-tax-transparent SARL into an entity-level taxed corporation — the option must be notified to the SIE and becomes irrevocable after five tax years; (ii) election of corporate income tax grouping (intégration fiscale) for French subsidiaries at least 95% owned, allowing group-wide IS consolidation (Arts. 223 A et seq. CGI); (iii) hybrid mismatch alignment under the ATAD implementation: France applies automatic re-characterization provisions of Arts. 209 B and 209 C CGI (deductible payments subject to a non-included counterparty income test), with mandatory disclosure of cross-border hybrid arrangements under DAC6 rather than elective check-the-box treatment; (iv) voluntary VAT registration election to waive the franchise en base de TVA (Art. 293 B, last paragraph CGI) enabling input VAT deduction and export zero-rating claims.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax — Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (TVA), governed by Arts. 256 to 289 CGI and the EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC; complements French customs duty regime (Code des douanes). Headline standard rate 20%; intermediate rates 10% and 5.5% apply only to narrow categories (pet food for animal feed qualifies for 5.5%, while non-edible pet supplies/grooming products attract 20%).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 85,000 annual turnover for tangible goods (franchise en base de TVA, Art. 293 B CGI) and EUR 37,500 for services; EUR 10,000 cumulative EU distance-selling threshold below which distance sales remain taxed at origin (Art. 258 A CGI / Directive 2006/112/EC); operational note: an established e-commerce SARL distributing pet supplies from France is obliged to register for VAT from its first taxable transaction, as the exemption threshold only benefits micro-enterprises selling exclusively to domestic final consumers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing a mandatory structured e-invoicing and e-reporting regime (Decree No. 2023-1187 as amended by the 2024 finance law): from 1 September 2026 all large and mid-size enterprises must issue and receive structured e-invoices (Factur-X, UBL, CII) via certified Plateformes de Dématérialisation Partenaires (PDPs) connected to the central Portail Public de Facturation (PPF); from 1 September 2027 the same obligation extends to SMEs and micro-enterprises, including SARLs. The operating model is the 'Y-network' clearance hub: each issuer/receiver connects its PDP to the PPF through secure APIs (REST/JSON, SIREN-based routing, PEPPOL-style addressing), with real-time transmission of invoice metadata, payment data and B2C sales data (e-reporting) to the DGFiP. No 'digital stamping' postage scheme was retained — fiscal clearance is effected through structured-data exchange and the automatic presence of the PPF in the invoice flow rather than by stamping each PDF; nevertheless, each invoice issued by the SARL must satisfy the substantive TVA invoice conditions of Art. 289 CGI and Art. 242-1 B of Annex II, be retained in its original structured electronic format for at least 6 years, and electronic invoices must be received by the buyer in a format meeting the 3-corner integrity requirements.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies under Art. 262-I (1) CGI to tangible goods dispatched or transported outside the European Union by the seller or on its behalf — including pet-supplies sold by e-commerce and shipped from France directly to end consumers in third markets (Switzerland, UK, USA, APAC/Gulf states). Eligibility conditions: (i) the goods must be physically exported and the export evidenced by customs documentation (DAU/ECS declaration with MRN); (ii) the supply must be made to a non-EU acquirer/consignee; (iii) transport must leave the EU and the seller must hold proof of the effective export prior to or within the admissible evidence window (Art. 74-0 D, Annex III CGI); (iv) for offshore ancillary services, Art. 259-1 CGI zero-rates services directly related to exported goods (transport, loading, transit operations). Claiming the zero rate also requires a positive VAT posture (no franchise) so that any input VAT on French warehouse stocks and freight may be deducted; excess credits are refunded monthly/liquidated through the CA12 form and verified by the SIE.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration d'exportation via DELTA-X/ECS including the Movement Reference Number — MRN, plus the export summary declaration and any exit-confirmation receipt proving conveyance out of the EU)
Transport Document — Bill of Lading (Connaissement), Air Waybill, or CMR international road consignment note naming the exporter/consignee and non-EU destination
Inward Remittance Certificate — bank credit advice or PSP settlement statement (Stripe/PayPal) showing receipt of the proceeds in EUR and tied to the shipment/invoice
Commercial Invoice and Packing List — export invoice stating HS codes, Incoterms, quantities and precise export weights
Contract/purchase-order evidence and proof of non-EU customer identity (customer's VAT ID not required for a private consumer, but delivery address evidence outside the EU is mandatory)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The zero-rating is conditional on complete export substantiation; if the required bundle is not held by the filing date of the VAT return covering the export (deferred evidence not admitted beyond the regulatory window of Art. 74-0 D, Annex III CGI), the DGFiP retroactively re-imposes French VAT at 20% on the export consideration. On audit, failure of proof attracts the bad-faith penalty of 40% (Art. 1729 CGI) or 80% in cases of organized fraud/manoeuvres frauduleuses, plus monthly late interest of 0.20% (Art. 1727 CGI). Fraudulent export zero-rating schemes (fictitious dispatches, fabricated DAU/ECS declarations, sham invoices not backed by B/L or payment repatriation) may be prosecuted under Art. 1741 CGI as délit de fraude fiscale, punishable by imprisonment of up to 7 years and fines of up to EUR 250,000 for natural-person principals, and are subject to administrative clawbacks over the 3-year standard reprise period (6 years in fraud cases, Art. L.169 CGI) and customs penalties of up to three times the evaded duties under Arts. 410 and 414 Code des douanes.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) and the French Treasury (Direction Générale du Trésor) under the authority of the Ministry of Economy, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty; foreign exchange policy is coordinated with the European Central Bank (ECB) and the European Commission.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is a member of the Eurozone; the euro is fully convertible for both current and capital account transactions. There are no general exchange controls on capital movements within the EU, and profit remittances (dividends, branch profits) are freely transferable subject to standard corporate tax withholding and anti-abuse documentation. Non-resident shareholders may receive dividends without prior authorization, but must provide tax residency certificates to benefit from reduced withholding rates under tax treaties. For e-commerce operations, cross-border payments in EUR and major foreign currencies are unrestricted, but transactions with sanctioned jurisdictions (e.g., Russia, Belarus) are prohibited under EU/OFAC sanctions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender of export proceeds exists in France. Exporters are free to retain foreign currency earnings in bank accounts, subject to reporting obligations for statistical purposes (Banque de France's balance of payments reporting). For amounts exceeding €50,000 per transaction or equivalent, the exporter must report the transaction to the Banque de France via the electronic reporting system (Téléprocédure). There is no conversion ratio requirement; the exporter may hold or convert funds at market rates.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (Compte Courant) and optional Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account (Compte Courant) and optional Capital Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for cross-border e-commerce operations. French-regulated Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) such as Qonto, Shine, and Lydia (via Treezor) offer multi-currency accounts, SEPA and SWIFT transfers, and virtual IBANs. They are subject to ACPR (Prudential Supervision and Resolution Authority) oversight and are fully compliant for treasury operations. However, for large capital injections or complex trade finance (LCs), a traditional tier-1 bank is recommended. Offshore EMIs (e.g., UK-based or Singapore-based) are viable but may face friction with French tax authorities and local payment processors; they are not recommended as primary treasury accounts.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally required for the initial onboarding of a SARL's legal representatives (gérant) and beneficial owners. Most French banks mandate an in-person interview at a branch or a remote video conference with a notarized identity verification (e.g., via a French consulate or a certified digital identity provider). Remote opening is possible for non-resident directors if they hold a European Economic Area (EEA) passport and use a recognized e-signature service (e.g., DocuSign with eIDAS compliance). However, for a newly incorporated SARL with non-resident shareholders, banks often require a physical visit to the branch to complete the KYC interview and sign the account agreement. The use of a local registered agent (domiciliation) does not waive the physical presence requirement for the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial owner with high-risk jurisdiction nationality or tax residency (e.g., outside EU/EEA, or in a FATF grey-list country)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (1) Certified passport copies and proof of address; (2) Tax residency certificate from the owner's jurisdiction; (3) Source of wealth declaration with supporting documents (bank statements, sale of assets, employment contracts); (4) Business plan and forecasted transaction volumes; (5) Commercial contracts with suppliers and customers; (6) Proof of registration of the SARL with the French Trade and Companies Register (RCS) and a valid Kbis extract; (7) UBO declaration (Déclaration de bénéficiaires effectifs) filed with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume e-commerce transactions with rapid turnover and multiple cross-border counterparties (potential money laundering via trade mispricing)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (1) Detailed business model description including marketplace (e.g., Amazon, Cdiscount) and payment processor (Stripe, PayPal) agreements; (2) Historical transaction records from payment processors showing consistent average ticket size and low chargeback rates; (3) Supplier invoices and logistics contracts (e.g., with DHL, FedEx) to substantiate physical goods flow; (4) Tax registration (VAT number) and periodic VAT returns; (5) A formal AML/CFT internal policy (even if not legally required for small entities) and appointment of a compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of third-party payment processors (Stripe, PayPal) as primary collection channels, which may be viewed as layering if funds are not directly settled to the corporate bank account
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (1) Signed payment processing agreements showing settlement to the SARL's bank account; (2) Reconciliation reports from Stripe/PayPal matching daily sales to bank credits; (3) A letter from the payment processor confirming the merchant's identity and compliance status; (4) The SARL's website and marketing materials to prove legitimate e-commerce activity; (5) A clear treasury policy that all funds are swept daily to the corporate account.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For a French SARL, inbound capital injections (shareholder loans or equity contributions) must be routed via SWIFT MT103 or SEPA CT (for EUR) with a clear purpose code. For equity contributions, use the purpose code 'S301' (Investment in equity capital) or 'S302' (Investment in mutual funds) under the ECB's Balance of Payments (BoP) classification. For shareholder loans, use 'S401' (Loans and deposits). The bank will require a copy of the shareholders' resolution and the bank account statement of the contributing entity. For amounts exceeding EUR 10,000, the bank must report the transaction to the French Financial Intelligence Unit (TRACFIN) under the anti-money laundering directive. The funds must be credited to the SARL's operational account; a capital escrow account is not mandatory but may be used for proof of capital for certain commercial contracts.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade settlements (e.g., purchasing pet supplies from Chinese or EU suppliers), the primary clearing rails are: (1) SWIFT MT103 for cross-border wire transfers in EUR, USD, or CNY (subject to bank's currency availability); (2) SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst) for EU suppliers within the SEPA zone; (3) Commercial Letters of Credit (LC) via SWIFT MT700 for high-value or first-time supplier relationships, typically issued by the SARL's bank and advised through the supplier's bank. For e-commerce refunds to customers, use the same payment processor (Stripe/PayPal) or SEPA Direct Debit (SDD) for EU customers. All outbound payments must be accompanied by the correct purpose code (e.g., 'S401' for trade credit, 'S402' for advance payments) and supporting invoices to avoid delays.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX Forwards (non-deliverable and deliverable) with a licensed French bank or EU investment firm, subject to ISDA or local master agreement
FX Swaps (swap de change) for short-term liquidity management, permitted under French financial regulations
Currency Options (European-style) for hedging against adverse EUR/USD or EUR/CNY movements, available from tier-1 banks
Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swaps (CCIRS) if the SARL has long-term foreign currency debt, though not typical for e-commerce

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for exotic currencies (e.g., CNY) if the bank has a corresponding offshore market access; note that onshore CNY forwards are restricted for non-residents, but NDFs are permissible

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts Filing (Dépôt des Comptes Annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registrar of the Commercial Court / RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after financial year-end; for calendar-year SARL by 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of EUR 50–100; potential court order to file with additional fine up to EUR 2,000; repeated default may trigger administrative strike-off from RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Tax Return (Liasse Fiscale / Déclaration de Résultats)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Second business day after 1 May for calendar-year companies; adjusted for online filing in May
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 5% of tax due plus EUR 50 per return; 10% surcharge if unfiled after 30 days; daily interest; possible tax lien and legal prosecution.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory if the SARL exceeds at least two of three thresholds: total assets > EUR 4,000,000; annual turnover > EUR 8,000,000; average workforce > 50 employees. Lower thresholds apply for parent companies or if part of a group.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP under the Plan Comptable Général, per Article L123-13 and R123-172 of the French Commercial Code.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL must maintain a register of beneficial owners at the registered office and file a UBO declaration with the RCS, updating within 30 days of any shareholding or control change. No separate annual UBO confirmation filing exists, but the register must be certified as accurate at the annual general meeting approving the accounts.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (standard corporate income tax rate applicable to French branches and resident companies; reduced 15% rate applies to the first EUR 38,120 of taxable profit qualifying for the reduced SME rate)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced SME rate of 15% on the first EUR 38,120 of taxable profit (CGI art. 219-V); research tax credit (CIR) at 30% on eligible R&D expenses up to EUR 100 million; innovation tax credit (CII) at 20% for SME prototype expenses up to EUR 400,000; partial exemption for qualifying young innovative enterprises; no specific tax holiday for e-commerce resellers of pet products.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited carryforward, annual offset cap of EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of taxable profit exceeding EUR 1,000,000 (CGI art. 209-I); carryback allowed for 3 years subject to a capped amount of EUR 1,000,000,

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual corporate income tax return: Declaration of Result (Form Cerfa 2065-SD) with annexes Cerfa 2052 to 2067-SD and Transfer Pricing Annex 2059-SD; filed via the French EDI (télé-IR/EFI) system which is mandatory for all corporate taxpayers under CGI art. 1687-1.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months following the fiscal year-end. For a SARL closing on December 31, the practical EDI filing date is May 3; for other fiscal year-ends, the deadline is three months after closing. Quarterly instalment payments are due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December, with the final balance paid with the annual return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income or loss before allocation of carried-forward deficits; includes all business profits from electronically supplied pet product sales, after allowable deductions for e-commerce operating expenses, depreciation, stock costs, and write-offs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident-owned SARL with a French independent company files as a French tax resident company; all online revenues from French consumers are taxable in France. A foreign parent must not impute losses or profits from non-French activities into this box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box B1 / B2 (Cadre B - Déficits antérieurs)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Carry-forward of tax losses utilized in the current year. Limited to EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of taxable profit exceeding EUR 1,000,000. Carryback of prior year losses is reported subject to the three-year rule and EUR 1,000,000 cap.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only French-sourced tax losses of the French entity or branch may be carried forward. Foreign branch or parent company losses are not deductible against French taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box W1 / W2 (Crédits d'impôt et réductions)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of research tax credit, innovation tax credit, family tax credit, foreign tax credits, and withholding tax credits used against corporate income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies may claim credits only for taxes from French permanent establishments; treaty foreign tax credits must satisfy the OECD treaty provisions and cannot exceed the corresponding French CIT.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an automatic 10% increase of the tax due (CGI art. 1728-1); a formal notice unpaid for over 30 days adds a monthly 5% penalty up to 50%, plus late-payment interest at 0.20% per month. In cases of intentional concealment or fraud, the penalty increases to 40% to 80%, with criminal exposure up to EUR 500,000 and five years’ imprisonment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Instalment and Final Settlement forms: Cerfa 2571-SD (quarterly advance payment) and Cerfa 2575-SD (final settlement and balance); transmitted via TéléIR/EFI.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly instalments are due by 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December, calculated at 25% (or reduced 15% rate) of the prior year’s taxable income. The annual final balance is paid with the income tax return within three months of year-end (May 3 for calendar-year filers).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount of the instalment computed on the previous taxable year’s final CIT assessed, net of the reduced SME rate and tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-owned SARL must use a French bank account for the tax payment; no offset with DTA foreign tax credits until the annual return is filed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Difference between total annual CIT and quarterly installments already paid; adjusted for current-year events and tax credits claimed in boxes W1/W2.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the SARL is a permanent establishment of a non-resident foreign parent, the parent’s head office tax credits cannot reduce the French balance.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Non-payment of instalments within 30 days triggers a 10% late payment surcharge, monthly late-payment interest at 0.20% per month, plus a 5% increase applied by the tax authority; forged returns attract criminal sanctions under CGI arts. 1729 and 1741.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Dividends paid by a French SARL to non-resident corporate shareholders are subject to a statutory 25% withholding tax under CGI art. 187-1. Dividends paid to non-resident individuals are subject to a 12.8% withholding tax under CGI art. 119 bis-2, plus possible social levies. For an EU parent entity holding directly at least 10% of the societe’s capital for at least two years, the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive reduces the rate to 0%. Treaty relief may further reduce the corporate rate to 0%, 5%, or 10% depending on the residence clause of the relevant double taxation agreement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty relief, the foreign shareholder must provide the French paying company with an attestation of tax residence (Form 5001-SD) issued by the tax authority of the shareholder’s residence country before the dividend payment date. The paying company then applies the treaty rate or the EU Directive exemption. In cases where domestic WHT has been levied, a refund application must be filed by the shareholder with the French tax authorities within two years under CGI arts. 119-4 and 246, together with the Certificate 5001/5002 and documentary proof of entitlement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid to non-French residents are subject to a 33.33% statutory withholding tax under CGI art. 182-B, reduced by applicable tax treaties to 0-10% (EU Directive usually provides 0% for royalties paid to an EU-linked parent). Interest on ordinary commercial loans or advances paid to a non-resident lender is generally not subject to French withholding tax under domestic law, unless the lender is located in a non-cooperative state (ETNC), in which case a 50% or 75% surcharging witha tholding may apply; treaty protection generally limits interest WHT to 0% for arm’s length financial arrangements.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: A French SARL is required to prepare Local File and Master File documentation under CGI arts. L13AA and L23B if its annual turnover or gross assets exceed EUR 400,000,000, or if it directly or indirectly controls or is controlled by an entity with turnover/assets exceeding EUR 400,000,000. Smaller related-party cross-border transactions for an e-commerce pet-products SARL remain subject to arm’s length reporting on box 2059-B, but full documentation is not mandatory at lower turnover.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not operate a formal Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime for ordinary trading SARLs; however, the general anti-abuse rule (abus de droit) under CGI art. L64, the concept of person effectiivement gestionnaire, and the EU ATAD CFC rules require the French SARL to have real management, employees, business operations, and economic substance in France. Lacking substance, the tax authority may recharacterize the e-commerce revenues as belonging to a foreign parent or a de facto French permanent establishment and impose additional CIT, 80% penalties, and criminal sanctions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting taxable online sales revenue from PayPal/Stripe settlement statements; disguising French-generated e-commerce income as foreign-resident income; maintaining false books or underreporting gross margin to reduce the 25% CIT; failing to register or report VAT and introducing fabricated deductions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalty of 40% of unreported tax for intentional misconduct and 80% for abus de droit; monthly late-payment interest at 0.20%; restitution of all avoided taxes. Criminal sanction under CGI art. 1741: fine of up to EUR 500,000 and imprisonment of up to five years, plus temporary suspension of business activity and publication of the judgment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the SARL may be jointly and severally liable for fraudulent tax arrears and penalties under the doctrine of faute de gestion; personal assets may be seized, travel restrictions and a travel ban imposed, and criminal conviction can lead to a bar from management of any French company for up to five years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Incorporating or maintaining a French SARL with no real establishment, no independent staff, no actual management, and using the entity only to channel PayPal/Stripe payments or to create artificial French VAT registration for e-commerce activities of a foreign principal.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax avoidance doctrine invalidates the company as artificial; profits are reattributed to the foreign principal under CGI art. 155-A, and 80% abuse-of-right penalty is due on the reassessed income. In commercial law, the company may be annulled for lack of valid will and real capital, exposing the founders to civil damages and fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held liable for the reattributed tax attributable to the hidden foreign owner, and may be prohibited from managing any commercial entity for up to five years; in aggravated cases, the criminal court may sentence up to seven years’ imprisonment for obtaining tax clearance by fictitious acts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using PayPal/Stripe rails to process deposits for third-party suppliers or to split pet-product sale proceeds for other merchants without a payments institution licence or without carrying out proper customer due diligence and AML notices under Article L561-1 LMH; high-volume transfers of unexplained origin through the SARL bank account.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the French Monetary and Financial Code, acting as an unlicensed payment intermediary exposes the entity to a fine of up to EUR 375,000 and imprisonment of up to five years, alongside an order to stop the activity, seizure of funds, and freezing of payment accounts. The tax administration may apply a 25% penalty on any amounts deemed to be undeclared income from payment processing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally subject to criminal AML liability; conviction results in a travel ban, personal financial guarantees, the potential loss of banking facilities, and in serious cases the attachment of personal property.
